# Nintendo Switch OLED Starter Buying Guide & Retailer Comparison

This buying guide is based on live checks of official Nintendo technical specifications and support documentation, alongside live product pages across **Amazon**, **Target**, and **Walmart**.

---

## Part 1: Official Nintendo Switch OLED Compatibility & Hardware Rules

Before purchasing accessories, verify these official hardware specifications from Nintendo’s technical documentation:

1. **Screen Size & Factory Film (7.0 Inches vs. 6.2 Inches)**
   * **The Difference:** The Switch OLED features a 7.0-inch display, whereas the standard Nintendo Switch has a 6.2-inch display and the Switch Lite has a 5.5-inch display. Screen protectors made for the standard Switch **will not fit** the OLED model.
   * **Official Warning:** Nintendo pre-installs an "Anti-Scattering Adhesive Film" over the OLED glass at the factory to prevent glass splintering if dropped. **Do not attempt to peel this film off.** Third-party tempered glass screen protectors are designed to adhere directly on top of this film.
2. **Console Dimensions & Full-Width Kickstand**
   * The Switch OLED measures **4.0" H × 9.5" W × 0.55" D**, making it approximately **0.1 inches wider** than the original Switch (9.4").
   * The back features a full-width adjustable kickstand. Snap-on hard shell cases designed for the original narrow kickstand will block the OLED stand. Carrying travel cases must accommodate the extra 0.1-inch width.
3. **microSD Storage Specifications**
   * **Supported Types:** microSD (up to 2 GB), microSDHC (4 GB–32 GB), and microSDXC (64 GB–2 TB).
   * **Recommended Performance:** UHS-I (Ultra High Speed Phase I) compatible with read transfer speeds between **60 and 95 MB/s** (higher transfer speeds improve game load times).
   * **Crucial Rule:** Game save data is saved exclusively to the internal console storage (64 GB on OLED) and **cannot** be copied or saved to a microSD card. MicroSD storage is used for downloadable software, updates, DLC, and media captures.
4. **Power & Docking Profiles**
   * The official Nintendo Switch AC Adapter outputs **5.0V / 1.5A (7.5W)** and **15.0V / 2.6A (39W)** over USB Type-C.
   * The OLED Dock strictly requires a **15V / 2.6A USB-PD profile** to initiate TV-out mode. Standard 5V phone chargers can slowly charge the console in handheld mode while asleep, but will not power TV dock mode.
5. **Controller Compatibility**
   * Joy-Con controllers (L/R) and the Nintendo Switch Pro Controller are universally compatible across all Nintendo Switch models.

---

### Category 1: Screen Protectors (Must be 7.0" OLED Specific)

   * **Retailer:** Amazon

   * **Why Pick It Over Others:** Unbeatable value ($2.66 per protector), proven 9H surface hardness, oleophobic coating against smudges, and includes 3 protectors with application guide tabs.
2. **onn. Corning Glass Screen Protector for Nintendo Switch OLED with Application Tray**
   * **Price:** $14.93
   * **Retailer:** Walmart
   * **Compatibility:** Tailored for the 7.0" OLED screen; dock-safe profile.
   * **Why Pick It Over Others:** Uses genuine Corning aluminosilicate glass for superior impact resistance and includes a rigid plastic snap-on alignment tray for guaranteed bubble-free, straight installation.

   * **Retailer:** Amazon
   * **Compatibility:** 7.0" OLED specific; 0.33mm dock-friendly thickness.
   * **Why Pick It Over Others:** Offers 4 tempered glass protectors plus a physical auto-alignment frame tool for under $9, providing the most backup units if you share the console with kids.

1. **Orzly Carrying Case for Nintendo Switch OLED Console**
   * **Price:** $23.91
   * **Retailer:** Amazon
   * **Compatibility:** Specifically molded for the Switch OLED’s 9.5" length with Joy-Cons attached; also backwards compatible with standard Switch.
   * **Why Pick It Over Others:** Tough EVA hard shell exterior, soft micro-fiber interior, padded screen cover flap, integrated slots for 8 physical game cartridges, and a large zippered mesh pouch that easily holds extra Joy-Cons, cables, or earphones.

   * **Price:** $12.99

   * **Why Pick It Over Others:** The most economical secondary travel charger ($12.99) that specifically supports the Switch OLED dock's 15V TV mode requirement.

Can I use an SD card on Nintendo Switch?

No. Only microSD cards can be used on the Nintendo Switch console. Due to the slot size, SD cards and miniSD cards are not compatible with Nintendo Switch.

Can I use a microSD card on Nintendo Switch 2?

No. Only microSD Express cards can be used on the Nintendo Switch 2 console.

For more information on compatibility, please see microSD Card and microSD Express Card Compatibility.

Are microSD cards included with the Nintendo Switch system?

No, microSD cards are sold separately.

Which microSD cards are supported?

The following types of microSD cards are supported on Nintendo Switch:

microSD (up to 2 GB)
microSDHC (4 GB - 32 GB)
microSDXC (64 GB - 2 TB)

Important:In order to use a microSDXC card on the Nintendo Switch console, a system update is required.

In order to improve your gameplay experience, using a microSD card with a higher transfer speed is recommended.

High-speed microSD card recommendations:

UHS-I (Ultra High Speed Phase I) compatible
Transfer speed 60 - 95 MB/sec (the higher the transfer speed, the better gameplay experience on Nintendo Switch)
What information can be saved to a microSD card on Nintendo Switch?
Downloadable software
Software update data
Downloadable content (DLC)
Screenshots and captured videos

Important: Game save data is stored to the System Memory and cannot be copied or saved to a microSD card.

Can I move data from the system memory to a microSD card?

Screenshots and captured gameplay videos can be moved from the system memory to a microSD card, and vice versa. You can also transfer downloadable software if the system is updated to Version 10.0.0 or higher.

When a microSD card is inserted in the console, it becomes the default save location for downloadable software.

Game save data cannot be copied to a microSD card.

Can I use multiple microSD cards with my system?

We recommend using a single microSD card with your Nintendo Switch console. If you run out of space, you can copy over all the data to a larger microSD card.

Keep in mind that downloadable software saved to multiple microSD cards cannot be combined later into a single microSD card.

   * **Crucial Rule:** Game save data is saved exclusively to the internal console storage (64 GB on OLED) and **cannot** be copied or saved to a microSD card. MicroSD storage is used for downloadable software, updates, DLC, and media captures.
4. **Power & Docking Profiles**
   * The official Nintendo Switch AC Adapter outputs **5.0V / 1.5A (7.5W)** and **15.0V / 2.6A (39W)** over USB Type-C.
   * The OLED Dock strictly requires a **15V / 2.6A USB-PD profile** to initiate TV-out mode. Standard 5V phone chargers can slowly charge the console in handheld mode while asleep, but will not power TV dock mode.
5. **Controller Compatibility**
   * Joy-Con controllers (L/R) and the Nintendo Switch Pro Controller are universally compatible across all Nintendo Switch models.
